title: Instant new tab: keys typed right after Cmd-T all reach the focused New Tab field; after Cmd-W the next Cmd-T keeps every key again, in the first window and in a second one
preconditions: a fresh launch: one window, one workspace, one terminal tab with keyboard focus
converted from scripts/cmux-next/new-tab-e2e.py (plans/cmux-next/new-tab.md 2.3), which stays for its timing legs; tests/oracle/corpus/e2e/_scripts-094.json links them

steps.note: the settle lets the first spare page load and park
Cmd-T then 'hello' at once: the keys arrive before the page could report ready, so the New Tab key hold keeps them in order
Cmd-W closes the page; the settle covers the next spare loading
a second opening adopts the next spare and keeps every key the same way
the script's cross-window leg: a second window, whose Cmd-T reparents the one spare
debug.focus lists the window controllers in creation order (WindowManager.controllers), so windows/1/id is the second window; the script takes its debug.key window ids from the same list
Cmd-T and the keys sent to the second window by id: with no window debug.key picks the launch window, and the reparent never runs

invariants: focus at typed and typed-again resolves to the new New Tab page (an agentPage target) in the launch window: the field has the keyboard

focus at typed-in-second resolves to a new New Tab page in the window whose id window-ids read at windows/1, not in the launch window, and the launch window's tabs equal those at typed-again: the cross-window open adopted the spare there
the New Tab page's draft at typed, typed-again and typed-in-second is sha256 of 'hello': no key was lost or reordered (the script's 'no lost key')
the turn checkpoint of open-and-type already lists the new tab: the open lands in the key's own turn (instant create)
every mutation has one receipt or one typed error (I1)
ids stay stable unless the step created or closed them (I2)
teardown: quit the tagged app the run started
verify its debug socket is gone
untested: the main-thread time of an adoption (p95 under 16 ms), missed frames and the spare's WebContent footprint: timing, owned by the perf lab (scripts/perf-lab/stories.d/new-tab-page.json and the script's --bench and --bench-open legs), never an oracle value
whether an opening adopted a spare or was cold, and the spare retarget on a key-window change: debug.new_tab state only, which no facet records
typing in the same main-actor turn as the open (debug.new_tab open_and_type): debug.key sends one request per keystroke
